I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the cropping pattern that fits my land, water, and the market I know best. I will keep most of my land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because that is the safest way for me to use the full year, spread risk, and get steady grain output. Wheat goes through the cool season well here, and maize follows after wheat harvest and makes good use of the summer heat and rain. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, stronger disease resistance, and better yield than old saved seed. I will keep fertilizer moderate and practical: enough nitrogen to push growth, phosphorus to support roots and grain filling, and potassium to hold plant strength, but not so much that I waste money. I will plough before wheat where I need to break the soil and bury residues, and I will use rotary tillage before summer maize so I can plant quickly after wheat harvest. I will irrigate wheat more times because spring drought is common for me, while maize will get fewer irrigations since summer rain usually helps. I will spray only as needed but I will still plan for a few pesticide applications to control weeds, aphids, rust, corn borer, and leaf diseases. This is the plan I would follow because it matches my area, my age, my experience, and the kind of work I can manage steadily through the whole season.
